High-intensity exercise requires rapid ATP production to sustain muscle contraction.  
If ATP demand exceeds the supply, ATP levels drop and ADP and inorganic phosphate accumulate, contributing to fatigue.  
Option (A) is incorrect because ADP concentration rises, not falls, during intense exercise.  
Option (B) is too vague — ATP production is not simply “inhibited” but rather cannot keep up with demand.  
Option (D) is unrelated to metabolic fatigue.  
Option (C) correctly describes the imbalance between ATP supply and demand as a fundamental cause of fatigue in high-intensity exercise.  

Final answer: (C)
